newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai paper industry hit by economic, export woes.
newsitem.headline: Thai paper industry hit by economic, export woes.

text.p: Thailand's pulp and paper industry woes are expected to continue into next year as slowing economic and export growth will continue to crimp local demand for paper packaging, analysts said on Wednesday.

"It is likely that the pulp and paper industry next year will be more sluggish than this year. The industry is closely tied to economic and export growth," Phaskorn Buranawit, permanent secretary at the Federation of Pulp and Paper, told Reuters.

Thailand's once-robust economy has slowed substantially with private economists projecting growth below seven percent this year, compared with an average of almost nine percent annual growth over the past decade.
Phaskorn said the paper and pulp industry had been growing by at least 12 percent per year for the past few years, but slumping exports this year will slow growth.
"The lacklustre exports have a direct impact on the industry. The (pulp and paper industry's) growth this year is likely to be around 9-10 percent," he said.
Paper products are used heavily in the packaging for exported electronics, food, and shoes, he said.
Thailand's exports from January to August totalled 930 billion baht ($37.2 billion) -- a meagre 3.1 percent increase over the same period last year.
Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan said recently that Thai exports for all of 1996 will not grow more than 5.0 percent, compared with robust 23.6 percent growth in 1995.
Pulp and paper firms have also been affected by a sharp fall in world prices of their products. Prices are expected to remain weak in the near term, analysts said.

Phoenix Pulp and Paper Plc, Thailand's largest paper company, posted a net loss of 191.5 million baht in the first six months of this year compared with a 585.2 million baht profit in the same period last year.
Siam Pulp and Paper Plc earned 101.9 million baht in the first half, against 278.68 million baht last year.
